content:
Last week, Apple sued OpenAI, accusing a former employee of stealing trade secrets "for the benefit of OpenAI."

It is reported that during the litigation process, Apple directly contacted several former employees who are currently working at OpenAI.

According to the Financial Times, Apple has issued evidence preservation letters to approximately 40 former employees.

An evidence preservation letter is a formal written notice sent to an individual or organisation, requiring them to preserve documents, records and other evidence related to a legal dispute. Such letters typically specify the particular items that need to be preserved.

This move stems from Apple's suspicion that the alleged trade secret theft may involve far more people than the single individual named in last week's initial lawsuit.

In short, Apple's lawsuit names OpenAI, io Products, and former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan as defendants.

You can read more about Apple's case against OpenAI:

  • Apple sues OpenAI, accusing former employee of stealing trade secrets
  • An email accidentally derailed pre-litigation negotiations between Apple and OpenAI
  • Apple's complaint reveals the number of former employees currently working at OpenAI
  • OpenAI says it has seen no evidence to support Apple's allegations of trade secret theft
  • Apple's lawsuit has not affected OpenAI's hardware release timeline
